clue.text: My remark upset monarch, such as Old King Cole

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of the words my and remark are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: Someone worries that a careless remark has offended the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is the anagram signal, not an emotion. Old King Cole is the 'merry old soul' of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Old King Cole is the nursery rhyme's jolly reveller, an example of someone given to festive fun.

clue.text: Clearing former partner, I have one informer imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned says the one-and-informer pair is locked up inside the outer pieces

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
I have contracts to I've
taken as written
a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: Someone is cleared after their ex and an informer end up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: EX and IVE together surround ONE and RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something that frees a person from blame, as in clearing their name.

clue.text: Again sends away for about 100 instruments

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the hundred sits within the reorder word

parts.note: to reorder is to send away for again
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A music shop reorders a hundred instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorders are wooden woodwind pipes, a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Bound to be in this country?

definitions.text: Bound to be in this country?

parts.words: Bound to be in this country?
parts.note: reads as a certainty about where someone will be, but books may be bound in a fine goatskin leather named after a North African kingdom

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' is the bookbinder's word: fine books are bound in this leather.
explanation.definitionFit: The North African kingdom gives its name to a goatskin leather used for binding books.

clue.text: One doesn't need to be a thought-reader to be so decisive

definitions.text: One doesn't need to be a thought-reader to be so decisive

parts.words: One doesn't need to be a thought-reader to be so decisive
parts.note: a decisive person is certain of their own intentions, which needs no mind-reading skill, only awareness of one's own thoughts

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being firm and decided in one's opinions, without wavering.

clue.text: Narration given in unusually clear Italian

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of clear plus the Italian are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A story is told in remarkably clear Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is an account or telling of events, a narration.

clue.text: Mirror's backing for one person, in contrast to another

definitions.meaning: thin metal sheet laid behind the glass of a looking-glass

definitions.text: one person, in contrast to another
definitions.meaning: a character who sets off another by contrast, as a straight man does a comic

explanation.surface: Someone describes the silvering of a mirror and a contrasting partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal leaf backs a mirror; a contrasting character sets off a companion.

clue.text: Ship's captain under particular king or queen

indicators.note: in a down answer the first word sits above the second, so it is under it

parts.note: own means particular to oneself, as in one's own room
ER, Elizabeth Regina or Edwardus Rex, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A ship's captain serves under a particular monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Owner' is old Royal Navy slang for the captain of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval slang: sailors traditionally called their commanding officer the owner.

clue.text: Union leader a great deal in evidence around this plant

indicators.note: around says the great deal wraps round the union's leading letter

parts.note: lots means a great deal

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of union

explanation.surface: A trade union leader is much in evidence around a certain plant.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside LOTS; 'in evidence' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a flowering aquatic plant.

clue.text: Affair not new to Emperor, perhaps

indicators.note: not new tells us to drop N, the abbreviation for new, from the affair word

parts.note: a concern is an affair or business
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scandal that is not news to the Emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: CONCERN loses N for 'not new', then TO. Beethoven's Piano Concerto No 5 is nicknamed the Emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's fifth piano work of this kind is nicknamed the Emperor, so it is an example.

clue.text: Instrument given variation in middle of 10

indicators.note: given variation says the letters are varied in their order
middle of means the word without its first and last letters

parts.note: refers to the answer at 10 across

explanation.surface: An instrument has a varied part in the middle of the concerto.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of CONCERTO is ONCERT, which 'given variation' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornet is a brass wind instrument like a small trumpet.

clue.text: Most of passenger ship one constructed, initially, of iron

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the ship word is dropped

parts.note: a ferry is a passenger ship
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of constructed

explanation.surface: A passenger ship was built mostly of iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferric is the chemist's adjective meaning containing or relating to iron.

clue.text: Devises interchanging sections for these defences

indicators.note: interchanging sections says the two halves of the devising phrase swap places

parts.note: works out means devises

explanation.surface: Someone devises a plan of swapping sections of the defences.
explanation.walkthrough: WORKS OUT has its two parts swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Outworks are minor fortifications built beyond a castle's main defensive walls.

clue.text: Retained Arab article about learner's urge to pick things up

indicators.note: about means the retained-Arab-article group goes around the learner

parts.note: kept means retained
L is the learner plate abbreviation
an Omani is an Arab from Oman
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An Arab keeps an article about a learner's compulsion to take things.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside KEPTOMANIA, after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Kleptomania is a compulsive craving to steal, a wry take on picking things up.

clue.text: Pursued animals full of fighting spirit

definitions.meaning: wild creatures hunted for sport or food
plucky and willing, as in up for it

explanation.surface: Hunted creatures show fighting spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunted quarry is called this; it also means plucky and willing to try.

clue.text: Had something in common drank too much?

definitions.meaning: read as lapped to excess, like a cat drinking more than enough

explanation.surface: Two people shared interests and both drank too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Shared some ground means partly coincided; whimsically, lapping excessively means drinking too much.

clue.text: Fare initially prepared in the form of cooked greens

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of prepared

parts.note: as means in the form of, in the role of

indicators.note: cooked suggests the greens are worked over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A dish prepared as cooked greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges GREENS into SENGER. 'Fare' looks like food, but here it means a paying traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A fare is a person who pays to ride in a taxi or bus, a paying traveller.

clue.text: They minutely examine a girl's mathematical instruments

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so Di's
sectors are old hinged rulers used for calculation

explanation.surface: A girl owns mathematical instruments for close examination.
explanation.walkthrough: A sector is an old drawing instrument: two hinged rulers marked with scales.
explanation.definitionFit: People who cut up specimens to study them closely examine things in fine detail.

clue.text: Drink greeting worker in islands

indicators.note: in places the greeting and worker inside the islands

parts.note: CI stands for the Channel Islands
hi is a greeting
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A drink is offered as a greeting to a worker in the islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, a drink.

clue.text: Son hears about daughter's progress

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: about means the hears word goes around the daughter

parts.note: a judge tries, or hears, a case
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A son hears about his daughter's progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hears' is in the legal sense: a court tries or hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are steps forward, as in making great strides, so progress.

clue.text: Replacement for third man

parts.note: reads like cricket's third man fielder, but refers to Genesis: Adam and Eve's third son, given in place of the murdered Abel

explanation.walkthrough: Third man is a cricket fielding position, the false trail; Genesis says Eve named Seth as appointed instead of Abel.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis presents Adam's third son as appointed instead of Abel, killed by Cain.

clue.text: Style of architecture, say, rejected by one in publication

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the say abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: in places the one inside the publication

parts.note: an organ is a publication, as in a party organ
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A building style, for example, is rejected by someone in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns EG to GE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgian architecture is the classical style of Britain under the four Georges, 1714 to 1830.

clue.text: Endlessly jealous king, like Creon

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the jealous word is cut off

parts.note: green means jealous, as in green with envy
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Creon is portrayed as an endlessly jealous king.
explanation.definitionFit: Creon is a king of Thebes in ancient Hellenic tragedy, so he is Hellenic.

clue.text: Cricket side's determined attack

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
set means determined, as in set on winning

explanation.surface: A cricket team launches a determined attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or attack, as well as a beginning.

clue.text: French city extra hard to spell?

definitions.text: French city extra hard to spell?

parts.words: French city extra hard to spell?
parts.note: the champagne city is spelt both with and without an H, so one spelling carries an extra hard letter

explanation.walkthrough: H stands for hard; the older English spelling of Reims adds it, making the name extra hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims is the older English spelling of Reims, a city in Champagne, northern France.

clue.text: Positions of two hands indicate standard required

parts.note: at bridge the four hands are seated North, South, East and West, so two of them are E and N
to sign is to indicate

explanation.surface: Clock hands are set to show the required standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' suggests a clock, but the hands are bridge players, named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, and a standard is likewise a flag.

clue.text: Very poor native almost put on short time

indicators.note: almost means the native word loses its last letter

parts.note: an indigene is a native
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A very poor local worker has almost been put on short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means lacking money and necessities, destitute.

clue.text: Aeroplane flown to see which way the wind blows?

definitions.meaning: old RAF slang for an aircraft

definitions.text: flown to see which way the wind blows?
definitions.meaning: a toy on a string is flown to test the breeze, and flying one means testing opinion

explanation.surface: A plane is flown to see which way the wind blows.
explanation.definitionFit: RAF slang named an aircraft this; the toy flown on a string tests the breeze.

clue.text: Confluence of River Test used for manufacturing enterprise

indicators.note: a confluence is where streams join, so the river joins the test

parts.note: the Indus is the great river of Pakistan
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Where the River Test joins another stream, factories spring up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a Hampshire river, the false trail; here 'Test' just means TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial describes anything relating to manufacturing industry.
